notes: Seven runs, seven rules, no verdict of not exercised. The standard is applied as in sweeps/2026-10-31/grades/macro-dsl-skill.json: validation in a @doc false function called from a one-line quote is clean under Keep quote blocks small; a route recorded by a direct attribute write inside get's quote is violated even when validation runs in the macro body; the use rule needs an admonition at the top of @moduledoc; __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them. Code.fetch_docs reports :hidden for both macros in all seven runs, including the four that omit @doc false on one or both (ajyaj, cjads, hpamd, tqgwh).

Close call, ajyaj Keep quote blocks small: line 58 writes the route with Module.put_attribute(__MODULE__, ...) rather than @tiny_router_routes. No run behind the two standard files used this form (grep of their tiny_router.ex files finds none). I held it to the same standard, violated: it is still a direct attribute write inside get's quote, no function of the package records the route, and validation sits in the macro body, which is the shape of 2026-10-31 skill-haiku-1.

Close call, cjads use rule: the only fault is that the admonition (lines 7-9) names the private :tiny_router_routes attribute. The two standard files never ruled on this, because no earlier admonition named one (grep of their tiny_router.ex files finds none). I graded it violated because macros.md says "List only changes to the caller's public API, not private attributes." and this line does exactly that. Placement and injected code are otherwise clean, so if the caller holds that sentence as minor, this one verdict flips to clean.

tpgjm's admonition (line 8) names the @before_compile hook. It is not counted: it is a reserved hook rather than a private attribute of the package, and the rule's own example names @behaviour the same way.

Compile-time dependencies verified with mix xref trace, one scratch Mix project per run: the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex (checked with cmp) plus empty MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/handlers.ex. All seven call Macro.expand_literals with function {:call, 2} in the caller env, and all seven report both handlers as (runtime). All seven compile under mix compile --warnings-as-errors with no warnings (Elixir 1.20.3).

Outside the seven rules, for the record: each project loaded with mix run, then Code.compile_string compiled a router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and one declaring get "/", "not a module". All fourteen fail while the router compiles, with CompileError in ajyaj and tqgwh and ArgumentError in the other five. All seven return routes in declaration order and match "/", "/users/42" and "/nope" correctly. Formatting and parentheses on the get calls are not graded, as the brief says.
